sources.cite: Direkcija za mere i dragocene metale (DMDM), «Pravila upotrebe i pisanja mernih jedinica i fizičkih veličina»: «Oznake mernih jedinica pišu se iza numeričkih vrednosti u izrazima za veličinu, ostavljajući razmak između numeričke vrednosti i oznake merne jedinice.»; «U novi red se ne sme preneti samo oznaka merne jedinice.»; primeri označeni kao ispravni: «2 kg, 3 kg i 4 kg», «80 mm • 25 mm • 50 mm», «lAl = 30 cm», «25 °C ± 5 °C». Uredba o zakonskim mernim jedinicama i načinu njihove upotrebe («Sl. glasnik RS», br. 132/2021), član 5: «Način pisanja mernih jedinica mora biti u skladu sa standardom SRPS EN ISO 80000.»
sources.note: beforeUnits = kg, cm, mm, °C (U+00B0 U+0043): each printed with a space after the number by the national metrology authority, which also states outright that the unit symbol must not be carried alone to a new line. A metrology source, not a language authority, so MEDIUM — the same footing as the form evidence of hr, sk and bg. Single-letter units are excluded as in hr, sk and bg. km, km/h, ha, min and the Cyrillic forms (кг, км) are not attested with a space and are not added. '%' is deliberately absent: BIPM SI Brochure 9th ed. §5.4.7 sets a space before it, but Serbian practice in print is closed up (Брборић and Новокмет, Књижевност и језик 64/3–4, 2017, «96%», «73,5%») and no Serbian norm was read. The engine therefore follows the practice by leaving it alone: «96%» stays closed, and a space the author typed before '%' is left as typed, neither bound nor removed. Corroborated, language-neutrally, by BIPM SI Brochure 9th ed. §5.4.3 (https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/41483022/SI-Brochure-9.pdf). Currency, afterSymbols, abbreviations, afterShortWords and initialBinding stay empty or none because no free source states a rule: Klikovac, Српска интерпункција, pp. 57–64 lists % and ° among signs of Пижурица и др. 2010 without any spacing rule; the Pravopis 2010 (paid) was not read. Operator decision (no paid sources, pick and pin). Retrieved 2026-11-06.
